<!-- agent-orchestration:issue-key=freeze-audit-20261018-account-state -->

## Summary and priority

**P1 — fix before the code/demo release is frozen. Applies to both the V1 and V2 frontend.**

After owner A signs out and owner B signs in in the same page, the Library can display A's previously loaded video cards while B's list request is pending. Those cards retain callbacks with A's job document, including its signed playback URL. Pending list responses are also not fenced against identity changes, so a late A response can repopulate the page after B signs in.

This is a client-side ownership/privacy defect. The audit reproduced previous-owner filenames and a playable card. It did **not** attempt real S3 playback or demonstrate a server-side owner-predicate bypass. A valid presigned URL is a capability, so retaining it in another owner's active interface matters even when fresh API requests enforce ownership.

## Audited revision and evidence

Audited default branch: `Main` at `d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e`, 18 October 2026. The local audit checkout `7ee3de5` differs only in README text; its application code is identical. The frontend file also has no diff between the accepted `project2-v1` tag and this Main revision.

Relevant code, using immutable source links:

- [`showSignedIn`, app.js:178](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/frontend/app.js#L178) increments `sessionGeneration`, changes `currentUser` and resets the active upload card, but does not reset Library/Admin data.
- [`showSignedOut`, app.js:208](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/frontend/app.js#L208) hides the app and unmounts players; it leaves list arrays, cards, filters and pagination state behind.
- [Library state, app.js:1300](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/frontend/app.js#L1300): `libraryJobs`, `libraryOffset`, `libraryFilter` are page-global.
- [Card callback, app.js:1346](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/frontend/app.js#L1346) captures the old job; [app.js:1494](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/frontend/app.js#L1494) mounts the captured playback capability.
- [`loadLibrary`, app.js:1514](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/frontend/app.js#L1514) applies responses without a session/owner guard, including after `await res.json()`.
- [`loadAdmin`, app.js:1655](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/frontend/app.js#L1655) has the same asynchronous-response pattern.
- [Frontend test bootstrap, app.test.js:27](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/frontend/app.test.js#L27) mostly forces `FLICKPOND_LEGACY_API=true`; new coverage must also exercise the default V1 route mode.

## User-facing reproduction

1. Sign in as A and load Library with a completed private video.
2. Sign out without refreshing the page.
3. Sign in as a different owner B.
4. Delay B's `GET /api/media/jobs?limit=...&offset=...` response, for example with a test-controlled deferred promise.
5. Open Library before that response completes.
6. Observe A's previous filename/card. Its play callback still holds A's job document.

A second important interleaving is: start A's list request, sign out, sign in as B, successfully load B's list, then resolve A's original response. The old result must not overwrite B's state. A late old-session 401/403/error must also not sign B out or switch B's view.

## Executed offline reproduction

Run from the repository root after the existing frontend dependencies are installed. This uses the real shipped HTML and unmodified `app.js` in installed jsdom. All HTTP responses are local stubs; the URL is synthetic. It does not launch a browser, services, a VM or AWS resources.

```sh
node --input-type=module <<'JS'
import {readFileSync} from 'node:fs';
import {JSDOM} from './frontend/node_modules/jsdom/lib/api.js';

const dom = new JSDOM(readFileSync('frontend/index.html', 'utf8'), {
  url: 'https://demo.example.test/', runScripts: 'outside-only'
});
const w = dom.window;
let identity = 'A';
let holdNext = false;
const response = (body, status = 200) => ({
  ok: status < 300, status, json: async () => body
});
w.fetch = async url => {
  if (url.endsWith('/auth/me') || url.endsWith('/auth/login')) {
    return response({id: identity, email: identity + '@example.test', role: 'user'});
  }
  if (url.endsWith('/auth/logout')) return response({}, 204);
  if (url.includes('/jobs?')) {
    if (holdNext) return new Promise(() => {});
    return response(identity === 'A' ? [{
      id: '11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111',
      filename: 'A-private.mp4', status: 'done',
      output_url: 'https://storage.example.test/private-mp4?signature=FAKE'
    }] : []);
  }
  throw Error('Unexpected request ' + url);
};
w.eval(readFileSync('frontend/app.js', 'utf8'));
const settle = () => new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 10));
await settle();
w.document.getElementById('nav-library').click();
await settle();
w.document.getElementById('logout').click();
await settle();
identity = 'B';
w.document.getElementById('auth-email').value = 'B@example.test';
w.document.getElementById('auth-password').value = 'test-password';
w.document.getElementById('auth-form').dispatchEvent(
  new w.Event('submit', {bubbles: true, cancelable: true})
);
await settle();
holdNext = true;
w.document.getElementById('nav-library').click();
await settle();
console.log(JSON.stringify({
  signedIn: w.document.getElementById('who').textContent,
  libraryVisible: !w.document.getElementById('view-library').hidden,
  cards: w.document.getElementById('library-grid').textContent,
  previousOwnerPlayable: !!w.document.querySelector('#library-grid .playable')
}));
dom.window.close();
JS
```

Observed:

```json
{"signedIn":"B@example.test","libraryVisible":true,"cards":"DoneA-private.mp4Edit","previousOwnerPlayable":true}
```

Expected: B's pending Library is empty/loading for B, with no A card, filename, playable capability or handler retained in the active view.

## Suggested repair

1. Add one explicit reset of identity-owned view state on sign-out and identity changes. Clear list arrays and rendered cards/rows, remove playback references, and reset pagination/filter/editor selection as appropriate.
2. Fence Library and Admin requests with the existing session generation and owner identity. Re-check after each asynchronous boundary, including JSON parsing, before applying data, errors, redirects, sign-out or loading-state changes.
3. Aborting pending fetches can help, but an abort alone does not replace the generation/owner check.
4. Coordinate with the separate list-error-state ticket because it touches the same loaders.

Preserve the existing owner-scoped unresolved upload/retry/edit intent handling. Clearing all remembered intents indiscriminately would break safe replay after uncertain delivery and same-owner re-login. The fix is to isolate displayed/active state, not discard the idempotency contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A → logout → B never displays A's filenames, cards, rows, editor content or captured output capability, even while B's response is held indefinitely.
- [ ] A late A success cannot repopulate Library/Admin after B signs in and loads B's data.
- [ ] A late A 401/403/network failure cannot sign B out, redirect B, clear B's successful list or apply an old-session error.
- [ ] Delayed JSON parsing is covered, not only delayed initial fetch completion.
- [ ] Operator A → ordinary user B retains no stale Admin rows or active preview.
- [ ] Playback is stopped on logout and prior-owner capability references are removed from active view state.
- [ ] Existing same-owner uncertain-intent replay and cross-owner intent isolation tests continue to pass.
- [ ] Regressions exercise default `/api/media` behavior; legacy coverage can remain as additional coverage.
- [ ] `make test-frontend` and the PR's required verification pass.

## Handoff

Estimated effort: 1–2 hours, plus normal review/CI. Related: #195, #229. This is a distinct defect, not a duplicate of the AWS security-proof ticket: it is a same-browser session-transition problem that an API-only two-user negative does not necessarily detect. Local reproduction and repair require no deployment or AWS operations. Keep the existing design and illustrations intact.

## Agent coordination

Companion ticket: #246 handles list-load errors in the same Library/Admin loaders. Implement the session/privacy boundary first and coordinate or combine the frontend changes to avoid conflicting edits. #246 is not a prerequisite for closing this P1.

## Summary and priority

**P1 — fix before freezing V2-live. Booked-session V1 without activity markers is unaffected.**

Direct public Processing retry/cancel requests can return success and commit durable work while the always-on idle gate still says the Processing domain is quiet. The next repair tick and scheduled launcher can therefore skip SQL until the approximately 30-minute full sweep, instead of discovering the mutation on the normal next tick.

The missing wiring has three parts: no activity touch in the public Processing API, no `ProcessingApi` entry among activity writers, and therefore no generated marker environment variables or writer permission for that function. Adding a Python call alone is insufficient.

## Audited revision and scope

`Main` at `d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e`, 18 October 2026; local audit revision `7ee3de5` has identical application code. The always-on changes are merged through #239/#240. The broader live acceptance remains #238.

Trigger: an integrator uses the published `/api/processing` mutation routes with a valid trusted actor. Normal web/Publisher mutations generally enter through Media, which already records activity; that does not make the direct Processing routes safe.

## Source evidence

- [Public API, v1_api.py:73](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/processing/v1_api.py#L73): `retry_owned` calls the transactional messaging mutation.

- [messaging.py:155](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/processing/messaging.py#L155) and [messaging.py:308](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/processing/messaging.py#L308): retry/cancel change owned lifecycle/outbox state.

- [handlers.py:28](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/processing/handlers.py#L28): repair returns `{"skipped":"idle"}` before opening SQL when the marker is quiet.
- [launcher_aws.py:148](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/processing/launcher_aws.py#L148): scheduled launcher also skips a quiet domain.
- [activity.py:39](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/runtime_support/activity.py#L39), [activity.py:99](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/runtime_support/activity.py#L99): a valid old quiet snapshot can remain usable for `MAX_QUIET_SECONDS = 1800`.
- Existing working pattern: [Media mutation activity middleware, main.py:64](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/media/main.py#L64), and Processing command consumer activity recording.

## Failure sequence

1. Processing has no due work and a recent quiet marker; an old failed/completed job remains in its database.
2. A valid owner directly retries the failed job, or cancels/deletes an owned job through the Processing API.
3. The transaction creates queued work, a result/projection update or cleanup state and the API returns 202/204.
4. The API has neither touched the marker nor been configured as a marker writer.
5. The next repair reads the old quiet snapshot and exits without publishing the new outbox work. The minute launcher can also skip.
6. With no intervening event to invalidate quietness, propagation can wait until the full sweep, about 30 minutes plus tick alignment.

The precise delay depends on snapshot age and other activity. The audit reproduced the accepted request followed by an incorrectly skipped repair, not a timed live 30-minute stall.

## Executed offline reproduction

This traverses the actual GatewayAdapter and public app, then calls the actual repair entry path. Only domain mutation/session dependencies and SSM transport are stubbed. It verifies the missing touch/skip behavior without SQL or AWS; real SQL staging is established by the source links above and must be exercised by the repair regression.

Run from the repository root:

```sh
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 .venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import asyncio, json, os, time
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, patch
from uuid import uuid4
from contracts.gateway import GatewayAdapter
from contracts.v1 import Actor
from processing import v1_api, handlers
from processing.config import get_settings, Settings
from processing.database import get_v1_session

class Ssm:
    def __init__(self):
        now = time.time()
        self.values = {'/t': str(now - 1000), '/q': f'{now - 300} {now + 1800}'}
        self.puts = []
    def get_parameter(self, Name):
        return {'Parameter': {'Value': self.values[Name]}}
    def put_parameter(self, **kwargs):
        self.puts.append(kwargs)
        self.values[kwargs['Name']] = kwargs['Value']

async def run():
    ssm = Ssm()
    app = v1_api.create_app()
    app.dependency_overrides[get_settings] = lambda: Settings(
        postgres_dsn='postgresql://runtime@unused/processing_db', database_tls=False
    )
    app.dependency_overrides[get_v1_session] = lambda: AsyncMock()
    owner, job = uuid4(), uuid4()
    operations = [('POST', f'/jobs/{job}/retry'), ('DELETE', f'/jobs/{job}')]
    for method, path in operations:
        mutation = AsyncMock(return_value={'status': 'queued'})
        event = {
            'version': '2.0', 'rawPath': '/api/processing' + path,
            'rawQueryString': '', 'headers': {'content-type': 'application/json'},
            'requestContext': {
                'http': {'method': method},
                'authorizer': {'lambda': Actor(str(owner), 'publisher').to_context()}
            },
            'body': json.dumps({'retry_request_id': str(uuid4())}) if method == 'POST' else None
        }
        environment = {
            'PROCESSING_ACTIVITY_TOUCHED_PARAMETER': '/t',
            'PROCESSING_ACTIVITY_QUIET_PARAMETER': '/q'
        }
        name = 'retry_owned' if method == 'POST' else 'cancel_owned'
        with patch.dict(os.environ, environment), \
             patch('runtime_support.activity._ssm_client', return_value=ssm), \
             patch.object(v1_api, name, mutation):
            response = await GatewayAdapter(app, service='processing').invoke(event)
            repair = await handlers.invoke({}, None, 'repair')
            print(json.dumps({
                'method': method, 'response': response['statusCode'],
                'mutation_calls': mutation.await_count, 'marker_writes': len(ssm.puts),
                'next_repair': repair
            }))
asyncio.run(run())
PY
```

Observed:

```json
{"method":"POST","response":202,"mutation_calls":1,"marker_writes":0,"next_repair":{"skipped":"idle"}}
{"method":"DELETE","response":204,"mutation_calls":1,"marker_writes":0,"next_repair":{"skipped":"idle"}}
```

Expected: before an accepted mutation can create pending SQL work, the domain's existing activity protocol is applied; the following repair cannot continue using the earlier quiet snapshot.

## Suggested repair

1. Include `ProcessingApi` in Processing's activity writer map so the always-on template gives it the touched/quiet parameter names and the narrow touched-marker write permission.
2. Reuse `Activity` to record mutating Processing API requests before their transaction commits. Use the existing caching and timing assumptions; do not duplicate a separate wake protocol.
3. Keep health/read-only requests free of activity writes and unnecessary SQL work. Preserve the no-marker V1 path.
4. Keep SQL/outbox authoritative. The API should not acquire broad queue permissions or start encoders itself just to hide this bug.
5. Regenerate `deploy/aws/v1/template.json` with the existing renderer if the source map changes: `.venv/bin/python -m scripts.aws.v1.definitions --output deploy/aws/v1/template.json`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A direct authorized retry from an idle/quiet state records activity before the mutation commits and is picked up by the normal repair/publication path.
- [ ] A direct authorized cancel from idle records activity and promptly exposes its result/cleanup work to repair.
- [ ] An integration regression uses real transactional mutation/outbox state with a quiet gate and proves the next pass sees pending work; checking a mocked `.touch()` call alone is insufficient.
- [ ] Offline API tests cover both routes and touch ordering; definition tests assert `ProcessingApiRole` writer membership, correctly scoped `ssm:PutParameter`, and conditional marker environment.
- [ ] `/health` and ordinary reads do not write activity markers; a genuinely idle domain can still skip SQL and pause.
- [ ] The booked-session/no-marker path retains its existing behavior and does not discover ambient AWS credentials.
- [ ] Wrong-owner/forbidden/invalid requests still obey existing authorization and transaction semantics.
- [ ] Idempotent retry, duplicate delivery, cancellation fencing and the three-encoder cap are preserved.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make test-v1`, `make test-aws-v1` and relevant local integration/required CI checks pass.

## Related limitation to keep explicit

`Activity.touch()` deliberately tolerates failed SSM writes. A failed marker write followed by a successful read of an old quiet value can still delay repair until the full sweep. That is a separate documented degraded-dependency trade-off (AD-27), even after this missing-writer defect is fixed. Do not describe this patch as proof of an unconditional 120-second V2 recovery guarantee; preserve the bound separately or document the exception accurately.

## Handoff

Estimate: 1–3 hours plus review/verification. Related: #195, #236, #237, #238; introduced in #239/#240. This ticket is a local code/template regression fix. It does not require deploying or changing AWS to reproduce, and it does not by itself complete the live acceptance checklist in #238. Keep the existing two-domain design, owned data and finite encoder model.

## Summary and priority

**P2 — small demo/integrator usability defect.** The primary Publisher examples and CLI help tell users to supply `/api` as the API base, but the active V1 Gateway contract requires `/api/media`. Following the examples constructs `/api/auth/login` and other retired paths, so a working deployment appears broken to a new integrator.

## Baseline and affected files

Audited Main: `d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e`, 18 October 2026. Application code is identical in local audit checkout `7ee3de5`.

- [Root README:123](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/README.md#L123): cloud examples use `https://<cloudfront-domain>/api`.
- [Publisher help, cli.py:33](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/publisher/cli.py#L33): `HTTPS public API, including /api`.
- [Publisher README:13](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/publisher/README.md#L13): the first instructions/examples use `/api`; a later V1 paragraph finally supplies `/api/media`.
- [client.py:67](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/publisher/client.py#L67) and authentication: relative paths are appended to the supplied base; no domain prefix is inserted automatically.
- [Active prefixes, contracts/gateway.py:18](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/contracts/gateway.py#L18): Media `/api/media`, Processing `/api/processing`.
- [Public login route, definitions.py:1569](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/scripts/aws/v1/definitions.py#L1569): `POST /api/media/auth/login`.

## Reproduction and actual/expected behavior

Given the documented command:

```sh
python -m publisher --base-url https://example.test/api --json login owner@example.test
```

Actual constructed request: `POST https://example.test/api/auth/login`.

Expected V1 request: `POST https://example.test/api/media/auth/login`.

Likewise, reservations, finalize, job status, retry, edit and delete are relative to the Media base, so fixing only the login example leaves other instructions misleading.

The URL construction was reproduced with the actual PublicClient and HTTPX MockTransport. The actual local Gateway also returns 404 for `/api/auth/login` before invoking any domain handler. No public endpoint or live credentials were used.

Runnable offline URL check, from the repository root:

```sh
.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
import httpx
from publisher.client import PublicClient

def respond(request):
    print(request.method, str(request.url))
    return httpx.Response(200, json={
        'id': '11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111',
        'email': 'owner@example.test', 'role': 'user'
    })

with TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
    for suffix in ('/api', '/api/media'):
        client = PublicClient(
            'https://example.test' + suffix,
            Path(folder) / ('cookies-' + suffix.replace('/', '-')),
            transport=httpx.MockTransport(respond)
        )
        try:
            client.authenticate('login', 'owner@example.test', 'synthetic-password')
        finally:
            client.close()
PY
```

Output:

```text
POST https://example.test/api/auth/login
POST https://example.test/api/media/auth/login
```

## Repair scope

Make `/api/media` the primary V1 base in root README, Publisher README and `--base-url` help. Review the active login/register/publish/status/output/retry/edit/delete examples for the same mismatch. Keep true pre-Gateway examples only in clearly identified historical context.

Do not add a new server alias, silently rewrite arbitrary URLs, or weaken HTTPS validation to accommodate a documentation error. Preserve global-option ordering, the independent-client import boundary and secure cookie/storage handling. The old `legacy_upload` regression surface is intentional and does not require migration in this ticket.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A reader of either primary README is immediately shown `https://<frontend-host>/api/media` for V1.
- [ ] `python -m publisher --help` describes the V1 base correctly.
- [ ] All active Media-client examples construct the existing `/api/media/*` contract; historical `/api` examples are clearly historical or corrected.
- [ ] Verify constructed login, reservation and job paths with the existing mock-client checks or an equivalent offline smoke. A real AWS run is unnecessary.
- [ ] Existing Publisher tests remain green. Add a regression only if it checks meaningful request behavior; a test that merely mirrors README text is unnecessary.
- [ ] No Gateway route, authentication, cookie, storage trust or client dependency changes are introduced solely for this correction.

Estimate: 15–25 minutes. Related: #180 and #192. Local documentation/help fix; keep original course/proposal documents and roadmap illustrations intact.

<!-- agent-orchestration:note-key=freeze-audit-20261018-publisher-wait-budget -->

## Companion easy win: bounded cloud polling guidance

The audit's quick-start improvement also includes a suitable cloud wait budget. `publisher/cli.py:60–61` defaults to 60 polls at a two-second interval; `publisher/client.py:229` sleeps between attempts. That is approximately two minutes of polling intervals **plus HTTP request time**, not a strict two-minute wall-clock deadline. A retained successful live smoke took 123.8 seconds to terminal, and other healthy cloud jobs can take longer because of intake, queueing and startup.

Give an explicit bounded example where appropriate, such as `publish ./videos --wait --max-polls 180 --interval 2`, and explain how to resume with `status ASSET_UUID --wait ...` using the accepted job ID. Poll exhaustion is not evidence that the job failed. Avoid suggesting that the user republish an already accepted file simply to keep watching it, because that can represent a new upload intent.

- [ ] Primary cloud examples explain the finite polling budget and allow an appropriate explicit override without promising a fixed wall-clock duration.
- [ ] The recovery example uses the existing accepted job ID/status command and preserves the idempotency/replay guidance.
- [ ] No endless retry loop or broad change to client defaults is introduced solely for documentation convenience.

Coordinate this existing ticket with #249 (current docs) and #254 (demo handoff). All audit bug/easy-win work is indexed in #258.

<!-- agent-orchestration:issue-key=freeze-audit-20261018-list-errors -->

## Summary and priority

**P2 — reliability/usability defect; small demo improvement.** Library and Admin list failures are rendered as an ordinary empty result. A transient 503, server error or network failure therefore tells a signed-in user that there are no videos, instead of explaining that the list could not be loaded. This can look like data loss during an Aurora resume or other temporary outage.

The account-switch privacy issue is a separate P1. Coordinate these fixes because both touch `loadLibrary`/`loadAdmin`; an error-state improvement must never preserve another owner's cached list.

## Audited revision and code

Main `d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e`, 18 October 2026; runtime code matches local audit `7ee3de5`.

- [`loadLibrary`, app.js:1514](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/frontend/app.js#L1514): for non-2xx other than 401, assigns `[]`; catch also assigns `[]`.
- [`renderLibrary`, app.js:1328](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/frontend/app.js#L1328): empty data shows the normal empty-library message.
- [`loadAdmin`, app.js:1655](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/frontend/app.js#L1655): same pattern, with separate 401/403 handling.
- [Existing tests, app.test.js:983](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/frontend/app.test.js#L983) explicitly expect an empty Library on a failed list request. Those expectations currently encode the misleading behavior.

## Reproduction

1. Start the page in its default V1 route mode and let `/api/media/auth/me` successfully identify the user.
2. Open Library.
3. Return 503 from `GET /api/media/jobs?limit=...&offset=...`, or reject that fetch with a network error.
4. Observe the ordinary empty state and no useful Library status message.
5. Repeat as an operator for `GET /api/media/admin/jobs?...`.

The Library 503 case was executed against unmodified `app.js` in jsdom. Observed: `library-empty` visible, list grid hidden, `library-status` text empty. Admin's matching behavior is established by source inspection; it was not separately exercised against a live deployment.

## Actual versus expected

Actual: successful `200 []` and an unavailable endpoint produce effectively the same UI result.

Expected: a successful empty list says there are no matching videos; a failed list says it could not be loaded, with a safe retry path. The page should not invent a job failure or imply that uploads were deleted.

## Suggested repair

- Represent loading, loaded-empty, loaded-with-data and failed-to-load separately for each list.
- Use a safe human-readable unavailable message. Do not put raw response bodies, signed URLs or internal diagnostics in the UI.
- Either keep clearly marked last-known data for the **same owner/session**, or replace it with an explicit error state. Do not silently present stale data as a successful current response.
- Offer a bounded user-triggered retry using the current filters/page. Avoid a new unbounded retry loop.
- Preserve intentional 401 sign-out and Admin 403 handling, subject to the session-generation fencing in the privacy fix.
- When a retry succeeds, clear the error and render the actual response.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `200 []` still produces the genuine empty-state message.
- [ ] HTTP 500/503, network rejection and malformed JSON produce an explicit safe list-load error, rather than a false successful empty result.
- [ ] User can retry and recover to the current page/filter result without reloading the whole app.
- [ ] Any retained list belongs to the current owner/session and is labelled stale/unavailable as appropriate.
- [ ] Old-session successes/errors cannot overwrite or sign out a new session; coordinate with the account-switch ticket.
- [ ] Current-session 401 and Admin 403 continue to behave intentionally.
- [ ] Add default-V1 frontend regressions for error → retry → successful empty/nonempty list, plus Admin behavior. Update the existing tests that bless false emptiness.
- [ ] `make test-frontend` and required PR verification pass.

Estimate: 20–40 minutes if combined with the privacy repair. Related: #192, #195. This concerns failure of Media's own list endpoint; #196's Processing consumer-outage proof is a different scenario and need not be reopened for this UI defect. No deployment, VM or live AWS repro is required.

## Agent coordination

Related P1: #243 covers prior-owner state and stale asynchronous responses. Coordinate both changes to `frontend/app.js`; any last-known-list policy must respect the owner/session boundary fixed there.

## Summary and priority

**P2 — reproducibility/demo handoff defect.** The root V1 quick-start presents `make setup` followed by `make v1-up` and browser-enabled `make verify-v1`, but a clean clone needs an additional pinned Moto environment and Chromium installation that the sequence does not provide.

The nested local-runtime document mentions `V1_MOTO_PYTHON`, but does not supply the missing creation recipe in the primary path. The generic browser installer also selects Firefox on Linux, while the V1 browser leg requires Chromium. A developer's existing primary-repository caches and CI's extra install steps can hide both gaps.

This ticket fixes dependency/bootstrap documentation and helper behavior. The separate interactive-demo ticket addresses serving the actual frontend and pumping work after dependencies are installed.

## Audited baseline and evidence

Main `d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e`, 18 October 2026. Local audit `7ee3de5` differs only in README text.

- [Root quick-start, README:55](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/README.md#L55): `make setup` → `make v1-up` → `make verify-v1 ... V1_BROWSER=1`.
- [setup.py:55](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/scripts/dev/setup.py#L55): locked Python extras and frontend dependencies are installed; no isolated `moto[server]==5.2.4` setup occurs.
- [setup.py:81](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/scripts/dev/setup.py#L81): browser binaries are installed only when the optional browser-install flag is used, through the generic helper.
- [v1_runtime.py:86](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/scripts/dev/v1_runtime.py#L86): uses `V1_MOTO_PYTHON` or `.cache/aws-test-tools/bin/python` in the primary Git repository; raises when absent.
- [browser.py:188](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/scripts/dev/browser.py#L188): installer chooses Chromium on macOS and Firefox otherwise.
- [V1 Chromium helper, v1_browser.py:196](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/scripts/dev/v1_browser.py#L196): V1 acceptance launches `playwright.chromium` with `channel="chromium"`.
- [Working CI install sequence, v1.yml:124](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/.github/workflows/v1.yml#L124): explicitly creates the isolated Moto venv, installs pinned Moto, and installs Chromium and Linux system dependencies.
- [local-runtime.md:11](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/docs/execution/aws/v1/local-runtime.md#L11) and its browser-install advice must match the final root recipe.

## Clean-environment reproduction

The audit confirmed this mismatch by source inspection; it did not perform a new full clone/install or start services. Reproduce in a **clean independent clone**, not a worktree that can reuse the primary repository's `.cache/aws-test-tools` through the shared Git directory.

1. Have the documented base tools (the project's Python/uv/Node versions, Docker Compose, FFmpeg/FFprobe) available.
2. Use a fresh clone of the audited Main revision with no project `.cache`, `.local` or inherited `V1_MOTO_PYTHON`.
3. Run the root README's `make setup`.
4. Before starting containers, inspect the Moto resolver:

```sh
.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
from scripts.dev.v1_runtime import moto_python
try:
    print(moto_python())
except ValueError as error:
    print(type(error).__name__ + ': ' + str(error))
PY
```

On that clean setup, the documented resolver error is:

```text
ValueError: Set V1_MOTO_PYTHON to a Python environment with moto[server]==5.2.4
```

5. Independently inspect browser installation. Installing the Playwright Python package does not install its browser binary. On Linux, the advertised generic `make browser-install` installs Firefox, which does not satisfy V1's Chromium launch.
6. Following `make verify-v1 ... V1_BROWSER=1` without Chromium fails rather than completing browser acceptance; it correctly must not silently skip the requested browser leg.

If reproducing through `make v1-up`, use a unique run ID and clean up only that partially created namespace with the existing teardown helper. Prefer the resolver check first, because it establishes the Moto gap without starting containers.

## Expected behavior and repair direction

Provide a complete, copyable primary V1 setup recipe or a scoped setup target that creates the isolated pinned Moto tools environment, exports the matching `V1_MOTO_PYTHON`, and installs the Chromium binary used by V1. State required Linux system libraries separately and accurately.

Reuse CI's proven dependency choices. Do not add Moto to production images or make a legacy Firefox workflow stop working. A V1-specific browser/bootstrap target is acceptable if that is the smallest compatible change. Keep the local runtime explicitly emulated and independent of AWS credentials.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fresh independent clone can follow the primary documented recipe without relying on another checkout's caches or unpublished coordinator setup.
- [ ] The recipe creates/selects a Python environment containing exactly the pinned Moto server version used by V1 and supplies a valid `V1_MOTO_PYTHON`.
- [ ] The recipe installs the Chromium binary required by the V1 browser leg on supported macOS/Linux paths; Linux system-library requirements are documented.
- [ ] Root README, local-runtime instructions and browser-helper docstrings agree; `make browser-install` is not advertised as satisfying Chromium on Linux unless it actually does.
- [ ] Browser-enabled acceptance remains a failure when the browser is missing, rather than silently reporting PASS/skip.
- [ ] A unique namespace can run `make v1-up`, `make verify-v1 FLOW=all V1_BROWSER=1`, and scoped `make v1-down`; retain the command/environment result for review.
- [ ] Existing user `.env`, dependency environments, other runtime namespaces and browser profiles are preserved. Production dependency/image contents remain unchanged unless independently required.

Estimate: about one hour for a clear setup/docs correction, plus meaningful fresh-environment verification. Related: #180, #190, #192. This is local runtime preparation, not approval to deploy or operate AWS/Alibaba. V1 verification needs no Lima VM; do not start the 8/8 scaling profile for this task.

## Agent coordination

Companion ticket: #248 supplies the interactive local web/worker handoff. Resolve this bootstrap recipe before claiming that #248 works from a clean independent clone.

Source evidence:

## Outcome and priority

**P2, about 30–60 minutes for precise claims plus 1–2 hours for a focused regression.** Align the documented V2 recovery contract with the existing best-effort activity-marker behavior and prove the specific degraded path locally. This is separate from #244's missing Processing API writer wiring and should not expand into a new broker, identity system or infrastructure programme.

## Evidence and distinction

Main `d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e`, audited 18 October 2026:

- [`runtime_support/activity.py:21–39`](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/runtime_support/activity.py#L21) describes the best-effort marker and sets `MAX_QUIET_SECONDS = 30 * 60`.
- [`Activity.touch():86–97`](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/runtime_support/activity.py#L86) logs a failed `PutParameter` and allows the request to proceed.
- [`quiet():99–111`](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/runtime_support/activity.py#L99) can subsequently read an older valid marker and skip SQL. Read failures themselves fail open to SQL; the interesting case is **failed write followed by healthy read of stale data**.
- [AD-27:437–438](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/docs/architecture/decisions.md#L437) acknowledges roughly 30 minutes after a lost touch. Tick alignment/invocation overhead should be stated when describing an end-to-end bound.
- Original lost-work repair target is 120 seconds; worker interruption target is 300 seconds. Existing local SQL tests and old AWS receipts exercise narrower conditions. The evidence index already distinguishes unmeasured AWS queue-loss timing and incomplete duplicate-output checks.
- #244 reproduces a different, unconditional missing-writer path: no SSM failure is needed. Fixing #244 alone does not prove the degraded-dependency contract here.

## Failure sequence to document/test

1. Domain is idle and has a recent valid quiet snapshot.
2. A correctly wired writer tries to record activity, but that marker write fails transiently.
3. The owning SQL transaction still commits pending outbox/work state, as the current design permits.
4. SSM reads recover. The next repair sees the old quiet snapshot, so it may skip SQL despite the committed work.
5. The snapshot ages out; the unconditional full sweep discovers the work. Other activity/events may recover sooner, but must not be assumed in the worst case.

The audit established the code/design behavior; it did not observe a timed production incident. Do not label an in-memory/fake-SSM regression as AWS evidence.

## Scoped resolution

Make the ordinary healthy-marker bounds and the lost-marker degraded behavior explicit in current runtime/ADR/evidence guidance. Retain the original proposal target as the comparison target, with conditions/limitations; do not rewrite it after seeing results or mark an unmeasured scenario PASS.

Add a deterministic local regression using a controlled clock and a fake SSM client that fails a write, then permits stale reads. Prefer traversing the handler gate and committed pending state so the test proves eventual discovery by the sweep, not just a constant or mocked method call. Reuse existing activity/SQL recovery helpers.

If preserving an unconditional shorter bound is chosen, that is an explicit follow-up change to failure/acceptance semantics and requires its own review. This easy-win ticket does not silently require failed marker writes to reject otherwise successful requests or keep Aurora permanently awake.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Current documentation distinguishes healthy operation, SSM read failure, lost marker write and #244's missing-writer defect.
- [ ] The original 120/300-second targets remain visible, with honest evidence and condition-specific limitations; no universal V2 recovery claim is copied from V1 acceptance.
- [ ] A meaningful local regression covers failed touch → committed pending state → recovered stale reads → skipped early tick → eventual sweep/discovery.
- [ ] Snapshot expiry/tick alignment, marker-refresh caching and a truly idle domain are covered without a wall-clock half-hour wait.
- [ ] Existing skip-SQL/auto-pause behavior, ownership, transaction/outbox semantics and no-marker V1 path are preserved unless a separately reviewed policy change is made.
- [ ] Evidence-index/ADR wording states which proof is local/simulated and which actual AWS failure checks are still NOT_RUN.
- [ ] New documentation does not claim that the #244 fix alone closes this separate degraded-dependency case.

Related: #236, #237, #238, #244 and the results-summary/current-docs tickets. Local documentation/testing requires no AWS API access, VM start or long experiment.

<!-- agent-orchestration:note-key=freeze-audit-20261018-easywin-coordination -->

## Agent coordination

Full handoff: #258. Coordinate the separate missing-writer fix #244 and shared activity tests. Keep the degraded-dependency claims aligned with #249/#252 without treating a local regression as AWS proof.
